findings.title: Opening the "/" list re-renders the New task page forever
findings.body:
The panel element is memoized on `[items, select, show]`, and `select` (line 228-239) depends on `onChangePrompt`. The page passes `onChangePrompt={edited(setPrompt)}` (app/spawn.tsx:1094), and `edited` (spawn.tsx:728) returns a new function on every `SpawnPage` render. The controls files forward it unchanged (spawn-composer-controls.ios.tsx:176), so there is no memo to stop it.

While the list is shown, the loop runs like this:
1. `SpawnPage` renders and hands the composer a new `onChangePrompt`.
2. `select` changes, so `skills.panel` is a new element.
3. The effect at line 100 calls `overlayHost({ panel, composerHeight })` with a new object.
4. That is `setSuggestionOverlay` in the page (spawn.tsx:705), which re-renders `SpawnPage` and returns to step 1.

The comment at line 240-241 says a new element each render "would loop". It does loop here, because the memo is defeated by the unstable callback. The composer tests don't catch it: they use a stable `onChangePrompt` and a stable `host`.

Fix: keep the latest `onChangePrompt` in the `latest` ref and make `select` stable (`useCallback(..., [])`). Alternatively wrap `edited(setPrompt)` in `useCallback` in spawn.tsx. Prefer the first, since the hook then no longer depends on how the caller builds its handlers.

findings.title: Host test uses a stable onChangePrompt, so it misses the render loop
findings.body: The test `hands the list to the page's host...` gives `baseProps` a single `onChangePrompt` and a stable `host`, and re-renders with the same function. The real page passes a new `onChangePrompt` on every render (spawn.tsx:1094). The test should re-render with a fresh `onChangePrompt` each time and assert that `host` isn't called again when nothing changed. That is the failure described in the finding on spawn-composer.tsx:242.

findings.title: A project's own skills are also stored as the agent-wide fallback
findings.body: The header comment says a project's own skills "belong to that project's tasks only". But `rememberChatSkills` also writes the list under the host+agent key on every call (line 25). `rememberedChatSkills` falls back to that key for any project with no list of its own (line 31). So project A's chat skills can show up in project B's New task "/" list, and in a standalone task's. Picking one there inserts a command that agent can't resolve. Consider storing the agent-wide key only when `projectId` is undefined, or filtering the fallback to non-project skills. If the leak is intended (so built-ins like `/compact` carry over), say so in the comment and note the trade-off.

findings.title: Comment for loadSkills is split from it by the overlay state
findings.body: The comment at lines 701-703 describes the skills loader and the Cloud exclusion. It is followed by an unrelated comment and the `suggestionOverlay` state (lines 704-705), and `loadSkills` comes after that. Move the first comment down to sit above `loadSkills`.

contracts.action: Open the "/" list on the New task page; the composer publishes its panel to the page through SpawnSuggestionHost
contracts.equivalent_path: ChatComposer's in-column suggestion panel (chat composer); the page-level overlay is new
contracts.before_after: The effect pushes `{panel, composerHeight}` to the page's `setSuggestionOverlay` whenever `skills.panel` changes. The panel is memoized on `select`, which depends on the unstable `onChangePrompt` from `edited(setPrompt)`.
contracts.visible_effect: The overlay should appear above the composer. With the unstable callback the page re-renders continuously while the list is open.
contracts.failure_mode: Infinite update loop (setState in an effect, re-render builds a new handler, new panel, effect again) while the list is shown.

contracts.action: Load skills for the "/" list: getAgentSkills over HTTP, cached 30s, merged with the remembered chat list
contracts.before_after: Reads the remembered list, then `cache.load`; a rejection is not cached (asyncValueCache.ts:72-74). On failure it returns the remembered list if non-empty, otherwise rethrows. A 404 maps to an empty list in api.ts:1127.
contracts.visible_effect: A failed load shows an empty list, via the composer's catch at spawn-composer.tsx:220. An unreachable machine with nothing remembered looks the same as a machine with no skills.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: the error becomes `[]` and the bare "/" shows the empty panel. A retry happens on the next open, since the failure is not cached.

contracts.action: Remember each chat's skills in a module-level Map and clear it when a machine is forgotten
contracts.equivalent_path: forgetRememberedTurnOptions in disconnect.ts, the existing per-session memory
contracts.before_after: The effect writes on every change of `conversation.skills`. `forgetPairedHost` and `forgetServer` call `forgetRememberedChatSkills()` next to `forgetRememberedTurnOptions()`. Both clear all hosts, as the turn-options path does.
contracts.visible_effect: A new task lists what the last chat of that agent on that machine reported, until the app restarts or a machine is forgotten.
contracts.failure_mode: The Map is in memory only, so the list is lost on restart. See the finding on rememberedSkills.ts:25 for the cross-project fallback.

summary: The new \"/\" skills list on the New task page has one blocker. Opening the list sends the page into an endless re-render, because the memoized panel depends on `onChangePrompt`, and the page builds a new `onChangePrompt` on every render. The composer tests don't catch it because they pass a stable callback. Two smaller points: a project's skills are also stored as the agent-wide fallback, so they can appear in other projects' lists, and one comment in `spawn.tsx` sits away from the code it describes. The API loader, cache, forget-on-disconnect wiring and the other tests look correct.
